exposure race · monte carlo · v0.2 · calibrated to 2025–26 incident data

Does the exploit arrive before your patch?

One race, resimulated every time you move a slider. On one side, when a working exploit exists for something you expose. On the other, when you have actually closed it. AI moves three things at once on the attacker's side, and the honest answer is that a third of the race is already over before your clock starts.

The race

you close it exploit exists before disclosure you lost

Day zero is the day a patch becomes available. Everything left of it is exploitation that began before you had anything to install. The hatched area is not decoration: it is ∫ fpatch(t)·Fexploit(t) dt, exactly the probability that a working exploit exists before you have closed the hole.

Where the year goes

Every critical vulnerability that lands in your exposed stack, and what happens to it. Most die at the first step. The step with the smallest drop is where you have the least defence.

What the model is anchored on

Coefficients are not invented where public data exists. These are the load-bearing ones. Disagree with any of them and the conclusion changes, which is the point of listing them.

Median time-to-exploit for n-days, 21 d → under 1 d across the AI slider
63 d (2018) → 32 d (2021–22) → ~5 d (2023, outlier-adjusted)
Mandiant M-Trends
Share exploited before a patch exists, 12% → 47%
29% of 2025 KEV additions exploited on or before CVE publication, up from 23.6%
VulnCheck
Share of published criticals ever exploited, default 7%
~6% of all published CVEs have been exploited in the wild
Cyentia/EPSS
Edge appliances patch slower and are exploited faster
median disclosure-to-mass-exploitation for edge devices is zero days; 54% of perimeter vulns fully remediated within the year
Verizon DBIR
Detection converts a compromise into an incident
median dwell 14 d (2025); eCrime breakout averages 29 minutes
M-Trends
Supply chain bypasses the patch cycle entirely
454,648 new malicious packages in 2025; one npm worm hit 500+ packages in days
Sonatype
What this is and is not. A structural model. It is built to show the shape of the relationship and to rank your own levers against each other, not to produce an authoritative percentage. Absolute numbers inherit the uncertainty of every input above and of the anchors below. Treat the ranking as the output and the headline figure as an order of magnitude. Three things the model does not contain: credential-based intrusion, insider action, and physical access. It answers one question only, about exploitation of things you expose. Runs entirely in this page.
